_doc: The AI gateway helpers every SDK runs (hosted AI gateway arc L-172, lane L8; plan docs/plans/hosted-ai-gateway-plan-2026-11-25.md section 8.2 L8, seam S4 docs/plans/hosted-ai-gateway/api-s4.md). Three pure functions. (1) base_url: the base URL a model client is given, resolved first set wins: the explicit argument (source argument), SUPERBASED_AI_GATEWAY_URL (source env), the organization's address org_url + /ai/<upstream> when the destination is online (source org), the machine's app lane from the discovery answer's local.app_lanes when the destination is local or both (source machine). The provider is the client family of S4: openai appends /v1, anthropic and azure_openai append nothing (their clients add the API path themselves). An explicit or env URL is the gateway's address for that client without the provider path; a URL that already ends in that path gets nothing appended. It must be http(s) with a host, no user info, query or fragment, and plain http only to a loopback host (the AI gateway key is sent there); a bad one is the problem bad_url, never a silent fall-through. With an explicit or env URL an upstream the caller named is returned as upstream_header (the X-SBO-Upstream header a single-org gateway without a path lane selects by); the org address and the machine lane carry the upstream in the path, so upstream_header is empty there. The upstream defaults to the provider (openai, anthropic); azure_openai has no default, so the org address and the machine lane need one (upstream_required). An upstream id matches ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,31}$ and is not v1 or v1beta (bad_upstream). Under destination online the machine lane is never used. local.app_lanes is a list of {id, base_url}; an entry that is not an object, has no string id or base_url, or whose base_url is not an http(s) loopback address with no user info, query or fragment is skipped; the first entry with the upstream's id wins. Nothing resolvable is not_configured. Each case gives provider, upstream (null: none), url (the explicit argument, null: none), env (SUPERBASED_AI_GATEWAY_URL, null: unset), destination, org_url (the resolved organization address, "": none) and local (the discovery answer's local object, null: no answer); want is {url, source, upstream_header} or {problem}. An absent upstream_header is "". (2) refusal: an AI gateway refusal read from one HTTP answer, or null. The gateway writes every refusal with a top-level reason; the planrefusal body of a plan refusal (L4) may instead carry its code as a top-level string error. Anything without either (a provider's own error relayed as is, a success, a body that is not a JSON object) is null; the parser never raises. kind comes from the code and the status together: budget_exceeded (402), model_not_allowed (403), admission_denied (403), plan_required (403), quota_exceeded (429 aigw_requests_quota_exceeded); any other code, or a known code on another status, is other. message is error.message when error is an object, else the top-level message, else error when it is a string other than the code (without any, the SDK's own default line is not compared). request_id is the X-SBO-Request-Id header, else request-id, else x-request-id ("" when none). retry_after_seconds is the Retry-After header in integer seconds (absent: none). budget is read for the code budget_exceeded: level, scope_id, unit, and remaining and cap from remaining_usd and cap_usd (unit usd) or remaining_tokens and cap_tokens (unit tokens), estimated; a field absent or of the wrong type is null (estimated false). plan_refusal is the plan refusal parser's reading of the same body (sdk/contract/plan-refusal-cases.json, with the AI gateway's code aigw_requests_quota_exceeded and allowance axes requests_monthly and concurrency) for the codes plan_required and aigw_requests_quota_exceeded when the body carries a non-empty upgrade_url; want gives its kind, code, upgrade_url and capability. Python runs these in sdk/python/tests/test_ai_gateway.py, TypeScript in sdk/typescript/test/aigateway.test.mjs, Go in sdk/go/aigateway_test.go, Java in sdk/java/src/test/java/app/superbased/sdk/AIGatewayTest.java. (3) api_key: the key a model client sends to a resolved endpoint (source and base_url as base_url answers them), from SUPERBASED_AI_GATEWAY_KEY (gateway_key, trimmed; null: unset). On the machine's app lane (source machine) it is none whatever the gateway key: the client keeps its own provider key, which the lane forwards, and the gateway key never reaches the lane. Otherwise it is the gateway key when one is set; on a loopback base_url with no gateway key it is none (the provider's own key, to a gateway on this machine); on any other address with no gateway key it is the problem no_key, so a provider's own key is never sent to a remote gateway. want is {key} (null: none, leave the client's own key option unset) or {problem}. A key the caller passes explicitly always wins and is not in the cases (Go and Java take none). Python runs these through the client factories' key rule, TypeScript through openAIOptions, Go through GatewayEndpoint.APIKey, Java through GatewayEndpoint.apiKey(). (4) From SDK 0.2.0 the organization's address may come from the SDK-held file (contracts/destination.md section 6a, SDK quickstart plan section 3.4, SDKQS-10): it is the same resolved org address, so the same answers; a case's from field (destination_source, org_url_source) and sdk_key_present are informational and the runners ignore them. The SDK key in that file is an ingest key and never an AI gateway key: with no gateway key a remote address is no_key.
